filtration_certificate.euler_identity: 6 Pf(M) = sum_(i<j) M_ij U_ij, U_ij = partial Pf / partial M_ij
proof: Every perfect-matching monomial of Pf contains 6 current entries, so Euler contraction multiplies each monomial by 6.
Each term M_ij U_ij has (q,T)=(6,5); division by 6 is allowed over QQ.
This proves Pf belongs to F_5. Assign the redundant scalar graph coordinate that degree.
Euler alone does not prove a lower bound: a degree 4 scalar would require additional lowering evidence, absent from this algebraic construction.

proof: The Pfaffians of order 4 are nonzero Higgs classes, so their R is 4.
J[1] acting on an order-5 Pfaffian gives a nonzero multiple of an order-4 Pfaffian. Goodness therefore forces R >= 4.
The order-5 Pfaffians vanish on the Higgs orbit, excluding R=5. Thus R=4.
J[1] acting on the scalar order-6 Pfaffian is nonzero, forcing R >= 4. The scalar vanishes on the Higgs branch, so R <= 5.
The exact norm has sign (-1)^4, excluding R=5. Thus the scalar Pfaffian also has R=4.

proof: The Pfaffians of order 4 are nonzero Higgs classes, so their R is 4.
J[1] acting on an order-5 Pfaffian gives a nonzero multiple of an order-4 Pfaffian. Goodness therefore forces R >= 4.
The order-5 Pfaffians vanish on the Higgs orbit, excluding R=5. Thus R=4.
J[1] acting on the scalar order-6 Pfaffian is nonzero, forcing R >= 4. The scalar vanishes on the Higgs branch, so R <= 5.
The exact norm has sign (-1)^4, excluding R=5. Thus the scalar Pfaffian also has R=4.
